prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and so showing how reallocation across firms shapes exporting, foreign investment and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed: I now prefer B010 as a single part, with Helpman and Melitz. In round 1 I put B032 first. Three of the weaknesses I listed against it have stayed unresolved through the exchange: the entry bundles two strands, the shift-share identification and persistence of the China-shock effects are still debated, and the credit for the task framework reaches names outside the ballot. Under common criteria of significance, attribution and maturity, B010 does better on the second and third without being weaker on the first. Melitz (2003) turned trade analysis from industries to firms. The model explains why only some firms export, why exporters differ systematically, and how liberalisation reallocates activity toward more productive firms, a channel for gains from trade distinct from comparative advantage and from scale and variety. Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extends this to exporting versus foreign direct investment, which supports a two-name credit that follows the intellectual structure. More than twenty years of firm-level evidence from many countries, much of it built from newly digitised customs and register data, has tested the mechanism and refined it. As an economic historian I value work that finds new ways of measuring and then explains what the measurements show, and this work does both. My move is not driven by the number of colleagues who prefer B010. The chair and several members themselves caution against treating that as merit. It follows from my own comparison of the credit structures and the evidence, and from the fact that the B010 reservations are about wording and omitted precursors, not about who the central contributors are. B032 remains a strong alternative, and I would not regard a B032 prize as a mistake.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is credit. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Hopenhayn in firm dynamics, are real precursors or parallel contributors who are not credited, and Redding is also omitted. The citation cannot hide that cost, and the scientific background would have to acknowledge those strands explicitly. The size of the selection-driven welfare gains depends on parametric assumptions such as Pareto productivity draws, so the prize should reward the qualitative mechanism and its tested implications, not a particular welfare number. Trade was recognised in 2008, and I do not think field balance should decide among candidates, but the Committee should still be satisfied that this is a distinct advance. Finally, B032 has the more direct causal evidence on who bears the costs of structural change, and a Committee that weights evidence of that kind above attribution clarity could reasonably rank it higher. I am giving up some of that on purpose.

responses.point: Hassler ranked B010 first with Helpman and Melitz. He argued that the firm-level evidence confirms the mechanism, that Redding is a later quantitative and spatial extension, and that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are precursors whose omission should be handled through wording and the scientific background. He also warned against a lifetime-achievement framing for Helpman. He also noted in round 1 that the B032 entry mixes the trade-shock work with the broader tasks agenda, and that point helped narrow my B032 set.
responses.response: I now agree with the core of your case, and the question you raise about the B032 entry is part of why I moved. On Redding, I accept that his main contribution is quantitative and spatial trade built on this base, and I would not add a third name. I would handle the precursors as you suggest. The citation should speak of firm heterogeneity, selection and reallocation, and the scientific background should credit the Bernard-Jensen exporter facts, Eaton-Kortum and Hopenhayn by name. I would add one point to your wording: the exporter facts came from new firm-level data, so the background should present the discovery as a model that explains newly measured facts. That framing keeps the award from looking like a priority ruling over the precursors. I would still call the attribution workable, not fully resolved.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranked B032 third and proposed only Autor and Hanson, since the entry mixes two strands. She said the Committee must decide which strand it rewards before it can name people, and she accepted Katz as a defensible alternative to my choice of Dorn. She argued that B010 has a cleaner credit structure and a more settled empirical record.
responses.response: Your point is the main reason I changed my configuration. I had narrowed from Katz to Dorn to anchor the award on the trade-shock strand, but your account shows that this is still a choice the Committee would have to defend. Autor-Hanson, Autor-Hanson-Dorn and Autor-Hanson-Katz each credit a different strand, and the task framework also draws on Acemoglu, Restrepo, Levy and Murnane. On the chair's question, I do not have a principled way to choose between Dorn and Katz, since the first reflects the trade-shock designs and the second the long-run skill-demand framework. I read that as evidence that the entry is not yet a single unit for a prize. For B010 the question is narrower. I also agree with your point that a citation can reward the integrating framework without claiming priority over every earlier empirical fact.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B019 first. He argues that Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 mechanism is a single identifiable discovery with clean two-author attribution. He has moved toward treating B010 as a serious alternative, and he asked whether firm heterogeneity is a distinct advance beyond the 2008 recognition.
responses.response: I share your preference for a single clean mechanism, and I agree that the B019 credit is cleaner than anything on B032. I still place B019 below B010 for the reasons I gave in round 1. The direct empirical identification of the amplification channel is more indirect than the theory's influence, and the 2022 prize is thematically adjacent. On your distinctness concern, the new trade theory of 2008 gave symmetric firms, scale economies and intra-industry trade. Melitz adds predictions that representative-firm models do not generate, such as exporter premia, the extensive margin of who exports, entry and exit, and aggregate productivity gains from within-industry reallocation. Those predictions have been tested directly in firm-level data. If the Committee rejects that distinctness argument, I would turn to B019 with Kiyotaki and Moore before B032, because B019 has the cleaner credit.

responses.point: Strömberg ranked B032 fourth. He valued the well-identified designs and policy salience, but he worried about overlap between Katz and the 2023 prize for Goldin, the antecedents outside the list, and the contested longer-run conclusions. He now says he is not fully settled on the order of B019 and B010.
responses.response: I accepted your overlap and antecedent concerns in round 1, and they now weigh more with me, because they affect any version of B032 and not only the Katz one. I still hold that continued debate about magnitudes shows scrutiny, not fragility. But a prize rests more safely on a discovery whose central qualitative result is not disputed and whose credit is not contested. B010 meets that test better. On your B019 versus B010 ordering, I think the two are close in scientific substance, and the choice depends on how much weight the Committee gives to the breadth of firm-level confirmation against a single clean mechanism. I give the confirmation more weight, and I do not claim your ordering is wrong.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee accepts a two-name B010 citation that omits Redding and the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum and Hopenhayn precursors, and whether the scientific background can acknowledge them adequately.

How much of the qualitative selection and reallocation result, and of the gains from trade, survives productivity distributions other than Pareto. I am relying on my recollection of the literature here and have not verified it independently.
Whether B010 is judged a distinct advance beyond the 2008 new trade theory prize, since that judgment would shift my preference toward B019 or B032.

Whether my change of configuration undervalues the direct causal evidence in B032, whose central finding of slow and costly regional adjustment has survived re-examination, and whether a bundled entry that is hard to attribute is the wrong reason to rank it lower.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. I have no documented connection to Helpman, Melitz or the other credited names on B010, B032 or B019. My profile records only Lund colleagues and economic-history co-authors. I disclose, as a possible bias and not as a conflict, that my background in archival and measurement-heavy work may incline me toward research that builds new micro-data and tests theory against it, which describes both B010 and B032. My assessments rely on my own recollection of the literature and have not been independently verified.
